codeReview.summary: The feature implements the down command surface and most expected behaviors (ordered stop flow, selective tier handling, stale/corrupt PID cleanup, and idle no-op), but it has a blocking shutdown-accountability gap: the command can report success and remove PID files even when a process may still be alive after forced termination.

issues.description: stop_service() always removes the PID file and returns a ShutdownResult after _terminate_process(), but _terminate_process() returns false both when SIGKILL succeeds and when the process still remains alive. This means down can report a service as stopped and clear its PID tracking without confirming termination, violating the expected post-down guarantee of zero running managed processes/confirmed termination before cleanup.

Tier validation is skipped when stack tier metadata cannot be loaded (the check is gated by `if valid_tiers and ...`). In that case, `down --tier <typo>` silently degrades to not-running behavior instead of returning the documented invalid-tier error with valid tier guidance.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Feature metadata requires skillName `cli-feature`, but workers cannot invoke it in runtime even though the skill file exists in-repo, causing repeated procedure drift.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: worker-transcripts.jsonl (session ce99eb98-4412-4b8d-81ee-c7e67867f213) shows `Error: Skill "cli-feature" not found`; skill file exists at .factory/skills/cli-feature/SKILL.md; handoff.skillFeedback.deviations documents the same mismatch.

summary: Reviewed feature down-command via handoff, transcript skeleton, skill file, and commit b377667 diff. Result is FAIL due to a blocking termination-confirmation gap that can leave live processes untracked after down; one additional non-blocking tier-validation edge case was noted.
